q: Which channel sizes break out most, and are their audiences happy? Give n.
a:
Small channels break out most, and their audiences are mildly positive. Mid-size audiences are the happiest.

- Small: 36% outperformers (89 videos with a baseline, of 110). Net sentiment is +6 (39% positive, 33% negative) across 2,723 product-side comments.
- Mid: 22% outperformers (n=50 with a baseline, of 51 videos). Net sentiment is +11 (42% positive, 31% negative) across 2,358 comments.
- Large: 5% outperformers (n=38 with a baseline, of 51 videos). Net sentiment is about -3 (36% positive, 39% negative) across 1,965 comments.

Average relative lift follows the same order: about 8.0 for small, 3.7 for mid and 1.3 for large.

Caveat: the mid and large video counts are modest, and the sentiment gaps are small. Treat these as associations in a comment sample, not causes.
sql: WITH vids AS (SELECT c.video_id, CASE WHEN cr.tier IN ('nano <50k','micro 50-250k') THEN 'small' WHEN cr.tier='mid 250k-1M' THEN 'mid' WHEN cr.tier IN ('macro 1-5M','mega 5M+') THEN 'large' END AS size_grp, p.outperformer, p.rel_lift FROM content c JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official'), lift AS (SELECT size_grp, COUNT(*) AS n_videos, COUNT(outperformer) AS n_with_baseline, ROUND(AVG(outperformer),3) AS outperformer_rate, ROUND(AVG(rel_lift),3) AS avg_rel_lift FROM vids GROUP BY size_grp), sent AS (SELECT v.size_grp, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive'),3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS pct_negative, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive')-AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS net_raw FROM comments m JOIN vids v ON v.video_id=m.video_id WHERE m.lang='en' AND m.trivial=0 AND m.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') GROUP BY v.size_grp) SELECT l.size_grp, l.n_videos, l.n_with_baseline, l.outperformer_rate, l.avg_rel_lift, s.n_product_side, s.pct_positive, s.pct_negative, CASE WHEN s.n_product_side>=10 THEN s.net_raw END AS net_sentiment FROM lift l LEFT JOIN sent s ON s.size_grp=l.size_grp ORDER BY l.outperformer_rate DESC LIMIT 40

q: Which content formats work best for mid-sized channels?
a:
First impressions is the only format with a real sample that works well for mid-sized channels: 8 of 19 videos (42%) outperformed their baseline, with an average relative lift of 2.7 and net sentiment of +23 (n=1,050 product-side comments).

Full review and durability test both outperformed 100% of the time, but each has only 1 video, so treat them as anecdotes. Their net sentiment was +22 (n=60) and -20 (n=41).

Explainer/tips had a high average lift (9.7) but only 1 of 8 videos outperformed (13%), so a single hit probably drives the average. Net sentiment was -7 (n=326).

Comparison (6 videos), upgrade advice (8), meme short (4) and keynote recap (2) had no outperformers. Keynote recap sentiment was the weakest at -54 (n=79).

Caveat: these are associations from small video counts, not proof that a format causes the result.
sql: WITH v AS (SELECT c.video_id, c.format, p.rel_lift, p.outperformer FROM content c JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official' AND cr.tier='mid 250k-1M'), s AS (SELECT v.format, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, SUM(m.sentiment='positive') AS pos, SUM(m.sentiment='negative') AS neg FROM comments m JOIN v ON v.video_id=m.video_id WHERE m.lang='en' AND m.trivial=0 AND m.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') GROUP BY v.format) SELECT v.format, COUNT(*) AS n_videos, COUNT(v.outperformer) AS n_with_baseline, ROUND(AVG(v.outperformer),3) AS outperformer_rate, ROUND(AVG(v.rel_lift),3) AS avg_rel_lift, s.n_product_side, CASE WHEN s.n_product_side>=10 THEN ROUND(1.0*(s.pos-s.neg)/s.n_product_side,3) END AS net_sentiment FROM v LEFT JOIN s ON s.format=v.format GROUP BY v.format ORDER BY outperformer_rate DESC, avg_rel_lift DESC LIMIT 40

q: Which high-lift videos have the most negative audience reaction? Name two examples, with lift and sentiment shown separately.
a:
Two top examples: "iPhone Duo's Camera Disappears #shorts" (Time Travel Visuals) and "iPhone FOLD Hands-On | Apple COOKED!" (TechDroider).

The Camera Disappears short has a lift of 499.3 (72.9x relative lift) but a net sentiment of -60 (n=77), with 10% positive and 70% negative.

The TechDroider hands-on has a lift of 86.8 (12.7x relative) and a net sentiment of -52 (n=56), with 18% positive and 70% negative.

Both samples are reasonably sized. Lift and sentiment are separate measures here, so high reach doesn't mean approval. These are associations from a sample of comments, not proof of why viewers reacted this way.
sql: WITH s AS (SELECT video_id, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, AVG(sentiment='positive') AS pos, AVG(sentiment='negative') AS neg FROM comments WHERE lang='en' AND trivial=0 AND target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') GROUP BY video_id) SELECT c.video_id, c.title, cr.name AS creator, c.format, ROUND(p.lift,3) AS lift, ROUND(p.rel_lift,3) AS rel_lift, s.n_product_side, ROUND(s.pos,3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(s.neg,3) AS pct_negative, ROUND(s.pos-s.neg,3) AS net_sentiment FROM content c JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id JOIN s ON s.video_id=c.video_id WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official' AND p.outperformer=1 AND s.n_product_side>=10 ORDER BY net_sentiment ASC, p.rel_lift DESC LIMIT 10

q: Which audience topics are largest, and which are growing fastest this week?
a:
Samsung Did It First is the largest topic (n=1,061, 13.2% of comments) and is also growing, up from 98 to 285 comments week over week (share 12.3% to 14.1%). Next largest are Eager to Buy (n=572, 7.1%) and Praise for review quality (n=544, 6.8%).

Left-Handed Concerns is growing fastest. It went from 13 to 89 comments, and its share rose from 1.6% to 4.4% (+2.8 points). Eager to Buy (66 to 194, +1.3 points) and Waiting for Next Year (10 to 51, +1.3 points) also gained share.

Small-n spikes: No Face ID (1 to 14) and Reviewer's speaking style criticism (4 to 22) rose sharply, but the counts are too low to read much into.

Most topics grew in raw count, so share change is the better growth signal. This is a comment sample, so it shows associations, not causes.
sql: WITH base AS (SELECT c.comment_id, c.topic_id, c.day_since_launch AS d FROM comments c JOIN content v ON v.video_id=c.video_id WHERE v.topic='duo' AND v.format!='official' AND c.lang='en' AND c.trivial=0 AND c.topic_id IS NOT NULL), mx AS (SELECT MAX(d) AS m FROM base), agg AS (SELECT topic_id, COUNT(*) AS n_total, SUM(CASE WHEN d>m-7 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_this_week, SUM(CASE WHEN d<=m-7 AND d>m-14 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_prior_week FROM base, mx GROUP BY topic_id), tot AS (SELECT SUM(n_total) AS t_all, SUM(n_this_week) AS t_this, SUM(n_prior_week) AS t_prior FROM agg) SELECT t.topic_id, t.pool, t.name, t.origin, t.first_seen, a.n_total, ROUND(a.n_total*1.0/tot.t_all,3) AS share_all, a.n_this_week, a.n_prior_week, ROUND(a.n_this_week*1.0/NULLIF(tot.t_this,0),3) AS share_this_week, ROUND(a.n_prior_week*1.0/NULLIF(tot.t_prior,0),3) AS share_prior_week, ROUND(a.n_this_week*1.0/NULLIF(tot.t_this,0) - a.n_prior_week*1.0/NULLIF(tot.t_prior,0),3) AS share_change, ROUND(a.n_this_week*1.0/NULLIF(a.n_prior_week,0)-1,3) AS count_growth FROM agg a JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id=a.topic_id, tot ORDER BY a.n_total DESC LIMIT 40

q: How does audience sentiment on the iPhone Duo compare with the iPhone 18 Pro?
a:
The iPhone 18 Pro gets somewhat better sentiment overall. Its net is +12 (39% positive, 27% negative, n=3,482), against +5 for the Duo (39% positive, 34% negative, n=7,046). Positive shares are the same, so the gap comes from the Duo's higher negative share.

By target (Duo vs 18 Pro):
- Product: +14 (n=4,914) vs +19 (n=2,833)
- Competitor comparisons: +34 (n=826) vs +44 (n=234)
- Price/value: -57 (n=738) vs -46 (n=252), so the Duo is worse on price
- Apple brand: -32 (n=568) vs -64 (n=163), so the 18 Pro is worse here

The 18 Pro's brand and competitor figures rest on smaller samples (n=163 and n=234), so treat them cautiously. These are YouTube comments, not a representative sample of buyers.
sql: WITH c AS (SELECT ct.topic, cm.target, cm.sentiment FROM comments cm JOIN content ct ON ct.video_id=cm.video_id WHERE cm.lang='en' AND cm.trivial=0 AND cm.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') AND ct.format!='official' AND ct.topic IN ('duo','iphone_18_pro')), g AS (SELECT topic, 'all product-side' AS target, sentiment FROM c UNION ALL SELECT topic, target, sentiment FROM c) SELECT topic, target, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, ROUND(AVG(sentiment='positive'),3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(AVG(sentiment='neutral'),3) AS pct_neutral, ROUND(AVG(sentiment='negative'),3) AS pct_negative, CASE WHEN COUNT(*)>=10 THEN ROUND(AVG(sentiment='positive')-AVG(sentiment='negative'),3) END AS net_sentiment FROM g GROUP BY topic, target ORDER BY target!='all product-side', target, topic LIMIT 40

q: What do people like most about the Duo, and what do they criticise most?
a:
Buying excitement is the clearest like: the "Eager to Buy" topic has a net sentiment of +22 (n=572; 44.8% positive, 22.4% negative). Comparisons with Samsung's folding phones are also favourable at +15 (n=448; 47.3% positive, 32.1% negative).

The under-display camera draws the sharpest criticism, with a net of -18 (n=302; 23.8% positive, 41.7% negative). Price complaints are slightly negative at -5 (n=479; 35.7% positive, 41.1% negative). Durability doubts are about even at -2 (n=457).

The biggest topic, "Samsung Did It First," is evenly split at +1 (n=1,061; 39.8% positive, 39.1% negative).

Caveat: these are sampled English comments, and topics can overlap. The scores show the mood in each topic, not necessarily feelings about the phone itself.
sql: WITH base AS (SELECT c.sentiment, t.name FROM comments c JOIN content v ON v.video_id=c.video_id JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id=c.topic_id WHERE v.topic='duo' AND v.format!='official' AND c.lang='en' AND c.trivial=0 AND c.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') AND t.pool='product'), agg AS (SELECT name, COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(sentiment='positive') AS n_pos, SUM(sentiment='negative') AS n_neg FROM base GROUP BY name HAVING COUNT(*)>=10), liked AS (SELECT 'most_liked' AS side, name, n, n_pos, n_neg, ROUND(1.0*n_pos/n,3) AS pos_share, ROUND(1.0*n_neg/n,3) AS neg_share FROM agg ORDER BY n_pos DESC LIMIT 8), crit AS (SELECT 'most_criticised' AS side, name, n, n_pos, n_neg, ROUND(1.0*n_pos/n,3) AS pos_share, ROUND(1.0*n_neg/n,3) AS neg_share FROM agg ORDER BY n_neg DESC LIMIT 8) SELECT * FROM liked UNION ALL SELECT * FROM crit
